She also received a songwriting nomination in the Best R&B Song category for What You Need, alongside Ronald Banful. The nominations for the 69th edition of the awards were announced on Monday, November 16, by the Recording Academy. In the Best R&B Solo Performance category, Tems will compete against Beyoncé for Morning Dew (Donk), Kehlani for Out The Window, Victoria Monét for Let Me and Jill Scott for Pressha. Her nomination in the Best African Music Performance category places her alongside fellow Nigerian artistes Asake, Wizkid and Ayra Starr, as well as Ghanaian musician King Ayisoba and Beninese singer Angélique Kidjo. The category features Asake’s Gratitude, Aye Kan (Are You Coming Back?) by Kidjo and Ayra Starr, No Tradition, No Africa by King Ayisoba featuring Rocky Dawuni, Tems’ Big Daddy and Jogodo by Wizkid and Asake. Asake also earned a nomination for Best African Music Performance with Gratitude, while his collaboration with Wizkid, Jogodo, secured another place in the same category. Other African representation includes Angélique Kidjo, who received a nomination alongside Ayra Starr, while Nigerian singer-songwriter Tems remains among the continent’s prominent contenders. Meanwhile, British singer RAYE leads the overall nominations with 11, followed by Spanish singer ROSALÍA with nine. Ella Langley, Miranda Lambert, Olivia Rodrigo and Phoebe Bridgers each received seven nominations. Bruno Mars, Leon Thomas and Olivia Dean earned six nominations apiece. Other notable nominees include Taylor Swift, who earned nominations in major categories, and Nigerian-American singer Anitta, nominated for Best Latin Pop Album with Equilibrium. The 69th Grammy Awards ceremony is scheduled to be held on February 7, 2027, at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles, United States. The ceremony will be broadcast live on ABC and streamed on Disney+ and Hulu.
